paper.section: Appendix A: task definitions, metrics, validity checks, and final scores

selection: The website shows the best valid within-budget submission. These formulas define each candidate metric; independent post-budget final evaluations do not change the displayed results.

attn-qat.label: Effective TFLOPS
attn-qat.formula:
F = 26 × B × H × pairs × d_h
t = 2 × t_forward + t_backward
q_case = median₃(F / t / 10¹²)
score = √(G_video × G_LLM)
details: B is batch size, H query-head count, and d_h head size; pairs is S_q × S_kv, or S(S + 1)/2 under a causal mask. Times are in seconds; doubling forward time accounts for activation recomputation.
Each synthetic case takes the median throughput of three fresh-input trials after one warm-up, combining forward and backward time within each trial; a captured real layer is one timed step.

G_video and G_LLM are geometric means over each domain’s families: Wan2.1 1.3B and 14B, LTX-2, Kandinsky5, CogVideoX, HunyuanVideo and real video layers; LLM pretraining, long-context, fine-tuning, D = 256 and real LLM layers. Each family is the geometric mean of its recipe and sweep tiers; the two domains have equal weight.
Timing includes scheduling and synchronization; reference computation and validation are excluded.
conditions: NVFP4 fake quantization, outputs, and input gradients must satisfy FP32-reference checks.
All scored and correctness cases must preserve inputs and meet saved-intermediate storage bounds.

sources.paper: Appendix A: Attn-QAT NVFP4 Attention; eq:attnqat_metric and eq:operator_aggregation

wgrad.label: Effective TFLOPS
wgrad.formula:
F_trial = 2 × M × N × Σ_g K_g
q_case = median₃(F_trial / t_trial / 10¹²)
score = (G_large × G_many_groups × G_small_batch × G_sequence)^(1/4)
details: M and N are output dimensions; K_g is group g’s actual reduction length, drawn anew each trial. Times are in seconds.

Single-call cases use three trials and sequence cases three rounds of back-to-back calls, summing work over a round; each times the complete grouped computation and writes with the larger of synchronized host-wall and CUDA-event time.
Each family’s G averages cases geometrically per model, then across models; the large, many_groups, small_batch and sequence families have equal weight.
conditions: Grouped FP8 scaling and FP32 gradient accumulation must satisfy high-precision and BF16 references.
All scored and boundary cases must pass complete-write, input-preservation, and memory-safety checks.

sources.paper: Appendix A: K-grouped FP8 Wgrad; eq:wgrad_metric and eq:operator_aggregation

flux-moe.label: Effective TFLOPS
flux-moe.formula:
F = 2 × M × top_k × N × K / EP (summed over layers in sequence cases)
t_trial = max over ranks r of t_r
q_case = F / median₇(t_trial) / 10¹²
S_f = √(G_evidence × G_model) (or the one group’s GM)
score = (S_tp8 × S_tp4 × S_tp2 × S_ep × S_decode × S_sequence)^(1/6)
details: M is the total token count of the placement group, top_k experts per token, K input width, N output width per rank, and EP the expert-parallel degree. F is the mean per-rank matrix work and does not depend on the routing draw.
Each case uses seven trials after one warm-up and charges the slowest rank’s max(host wall, CUDA-event) time. Time includes all-gather, expert scatter, grouped multiplication, and synchronization.
Six families (tp8, tp4, tp2, ep, decode, sequence) have equal weight. In each family, evidence cases (paper and real tiers) and model cases each give a geometric mean, combined geometrically.
conditions: All scored and correctness cases must pass random-projection, FP32/BF16-reference accuracy and complete-write checks.
Preserve local and remote inputs, use fresh inputs, and satisfy rank-agreement checks.

sources.paper: Appendix A: Flux/Comet MoE Primitive; eq:moe_metric and eq:operator_aggregation

orpo.label: Training speedup
orpo.formula:
u = completion-target tokens / Σ₁₀_steps max(t_rank1, t_rank2)
r_row = median₄_pairs(u_candidate / u_TRL)
score = 100 × (r₁ × r₂ × r₃ × r₄ × r₅)^(1/5)
details: u is completion-target tokens/s across both ranks over ten optimizer steps, charging the slower rank per step and excluding warm-up.
Five TL;DR workloads each use four counterbalanced candidate/reference pairs. Take the median ratio per workload, then the equally weighted geometric mean.
The official TRL reference is remeasured on the same GPU pair with matching initial state and workload.
Timing covers forward, loss, backward, communication, and full-parameter update. A score of 100 denotes reference parity.
conditions: Loss trajectories, auxiliary outputs, gradients, optimizer states, and nonzero parameter updates must pass reference-relative checks.
Peak-memory, execution, and protocol checks must pass.

sources.paper: Appendix A: Training: Module Tasks / Qwen3 ORPO; eq:training_step_throughput and eq:orpo_metric

gkd.label: Training speedup
gkd.formula:
u = completion-target tokens / Σ₁₀_steps max(t_rank1, t_rank2)
r_row = median₄_pairs(u_candidate / u_TRL)
score = 100 × (r₁ × r₂ × r₃ × r₄ × r₅)^(1/5)
details: u counts answer-prediction targets across both ranks, including answer EOS and excluding prompt/padding. Ten complete steps are timed, charging the slower rank per step.
Five TL;DR workloads use four counterbalanced candidate/reference pairs after five warm-up steps. Take the median ratio per workload, then the equally weighted geometric mean.
The official TRL generalized-JSD reference is remeasured on the same GPU pair with matching initial models and workload.
Timing covers teacher/student forwards, projections, loss, student backward, communication, and update. A score of 100 denotes reference parity.
conditions: Loss, auxiliary outputs, gradients, and student updates must pass reference checks.
The teacher remains frozen; memory and execution checks must pass.

sources.paper: Appendix A: Training: Module Tasks / Qwen3 GKD; eq:training_step_throughput and eq:gkd_metric

opcd.label: Medical accuracy gain (pp/hour)
opcd.formula:
Δpp = 100 × (mean₃(a_final) − a_base)
score = 3600 × Δpp / D, if checks pass and Δpp ≥ 6.5
score = 0 otherwise
details: a_final and a_base are accuracy fractions. The student is evaluated on 2,436 held-out MedMCQA questions in three seeded repeats, without the medical system prompt.
The frozen original-model baseline is approximately 22.7285% under the same evaluation protocol.
D is audited seconds from first student generation through final weight publication, including learning and excluding model loading and authorized evaluation overhead.
conditions: Mean accuracy gain must be at least 6.5 percentage points.
Objective, teacher-probability, gradient, sample-use, and trained/published/evaluated-weight checks must pass.

sources.paper: Appendix A: Training: System Tasks / Miles Qwen3 OPCD; eq:training_quality_gain and eq:opcd_metric

opd.label: Math accuracy gain (pp/hour)
opd.formula:
Δpp = 100 × (mean₃(a_final) − a_base)
score = 3600 × Δpp / D, if checks pass and Δpp ≥ 1.6
score = 0 otherwise
details: a_final and a_base are accuracy fractions. The student is evaluated on 2,000 held-out DAPO-Math problems in three seeded repeats.
The frozen original-model baseline is approximately 25.9333% under the same evaluation protocol.
D is audited seconds from first student generation through final weight publication, including learning and excluding model loading and authorized evaluation overhead.
conditions: Mean accuracy gain must be at least 1.6 percentage points.
Student/teacher probabilities, sampled-token loss, gradients, sample use, and weight publication must pass correctness and provenance checks.

sources.paper: Appendix A: Training: System Tasks / Miles Qwen3 OPD; eq:training_quality_gain and eq:opd_metric

alfworld.label: Game-success gain (pp/hour)
alfworld.formula:
Δpp = 100 × (mean₃(s_final) − s_base)
score = 3600 × Δpp / D, if checks pass and Δpp ≥ 15
score = 0 otherwise
details: s_final and s_base are game-success fractions. The final policy is evaluated greedily on 1,134 held-out games in three repeats.
The frozen original-model baseline is approximately 25.1617% under the same evaluation protocol.
D is audited seconds from first training generation through final weight publication, including environment rollouts and learning, excluding model loading and authorized evaluation overhead.
conditions: Mean success-rate gain must be at least 15 percentage points.
Actions, rewards, token probabilities, advantages, optimizer updates, sample use, and published/evaluated weights must pass the required checks.

sources.paper: Appendix A: Training: System Tasks / Miles ALFWorld RL; eq:training_quality_gain and eq:alf_metric

sd35.label: Teacher-gap closure per replay hour
sd35.formula:
c_r = (q_student,r − q_base,r) / (q_teacher,r − q_base,r)
D = median(D₁, D₂, D₃)
score = 3600 × (c_OCR + c_PickScore) / (2 × D), if all gates pass
score = 0 otherwise
details: q is mean quality: normalized edit-distance OCR accuracy on 1,012 prompts or raw PickScore on 2,040 prompts.
Frozen original/teacher values are approximately (0.110282, 0.741047) for OCR and (19.911913, 21.597927) for PickScore. Both routes have equal weight.
Closure 1 matches teacher quality. D is median seconds across three replays; quality uses the real training run’s final LoRA and is evaluated separately.
conditions: Both routes must close at least 25% of their teacher gaps.
For each route, the mean of ln(KL_base / KL_final) over two paired repeats must reach 0.364 for OCR and 0.690 for PickScore.
Training-objective, gradient, optimizer, provenance, and publication checks must pass.

sources.paper: Appendix A: Miles SD3.5-M Multi-teacher OPD; eq:sd35_kl_gate and eq:sd35_metric

wan22.label: Fixed-workload replays per hour
wan22.formula:
D = median(D₁, D₂, D₃)
score = 3600 / D, if checks pass and mean_HPSv3 − h_base ≥ −0.28
score = 0 otherwise
details: D is median seconds across three fixed replays, each containing 16 prompts × 8 videos.
Replay timing includes reading, rewards, probability recomputation, training, logging, and weight publication. Loading, video generation, and quality evaluation are excluded.
The real training run’s final model is evaluated on 61 prompts × three seed groups. Video reward averages 0.1 × HPSv3 frame preference over frames 0, 4, and 8.
The frozen original-model mean reward h_base is approximately 0.789132.
conditions: Mean HPSv3 reward must be at least the original-model mean minus 0.28.
Frame rewards, sampling transitions, learning updates, and publication consistency/completion must pass.

sources.paper: Appendix A: Miles Wan2.2 DanceGRPO; eq:wan22_metric

grouped-fp8.label: Effective TFLOPS
grouped-fp8.formula:
F = 2 × N × K × Σg M_g
q_i = median of 5 trials [F / (10¹² × t)]  (sequence: median of 3 rounds)
G_f = GM(cases in family f), f ∈ {prefill, decode, latency, sequence}
score = (G_prefill × G_decode × G_latency × G_sequence)^(1/4)
details: M_g is expert g’s valid row count, N output width, and K the reduction dimension.

Each trial uses fresh row counts; compute throughput per trial before taking the five-trial median. Sequence cases time rounds of many consecutive calls, summing work over a round, and take the median of three rounds.
t is the larger of synchronized host-wall and CUDA-event seconds for dispatch, scaling, multiplication, conversion, writes, and synchronization. Preparation, validation, and warm-up are excluded.
GM denotes geometric mean. Cases have equal weight within each family, and the four families have equal weight.
conditions: All scored and correctness cases must pass.
Preserve block-scaled FP8 arithmetic, complete BF16 writes, input contents, and memory boundaries.
Timing and evaluation-integrity checks must pass.

sources.paper: Dynamic Grouped FP8 GEMM, main.tex:1489–1505; Shared Evaluation Conventions, main.tex:1232–1241

sparse-mla.label: Sparse-attention TFLOPS
sparse-mla.formula:
A_s = S_q × k  (or Σ topk_length)
F = 2 × H_q × A_s × (d_qk + 512)
q_i = median of 3 trials [F / (10¹² × t)]; stream: ΣF / Σt
G_family = √(G_evidence × G_sweep)
score = (G_V3.2 × G_GLM-5 × G_V4-Flash × G_V4-Pro)^(1/4)
details: S_q is query length, k selected keys per query, H_q query-head count, and d_qk query/key width. Values have width 512; F counts selected interactions.

Within each family, each group is the geometric mean of its cases; the evidence tier (anchor, trace, replay, multi, pattern) and sweep tier (sweep, heads, length) are geometric means of their groups. The four families have equal weight.

t is the larger of synchronized host-wall and CUDA-event seconds for the complete call, including scheduling, temporary allocations, computation, writes, and synchronization; streams time every call, compilation included.
Input preparation, reference checks, and warm-up are excluded.
conditions: All scored and correctness cases must pass.
Attention outputs, max_logits, and lse must satisfy sparse-index, duplicate-index, empty-row, and attention-sink semantics against independent references.
Preserve inputs and memory safety; use permitted BF16/FP16 multiplication with FP32 accumulation and softmax statistics.

sources.paper: Sparse-MLA Prefill, main.tex:1507–1523; Shared Evaluation Conventions, main.tex:1232–1241

paged-gqa.label: Attention TFLOPS
paged-gqa.formula:
A = Σb [S_q × L_b − S_q(S_q − 1)/2]
F = 4 × H_q × 128 × A
q_i = median of 3 trials [F / (10¹² × t)]; stream: ΣF / Σt
score = (G_decode × G_spec × G_long × G_stream)^(1/4)
details: L_b is request b’s cache length, S_q query length, and H_q query-head count. Head width is 128; A counts pairs allowed by the bottom-right causal mask.
The factor 4 counts QK and PV multiply-add work; timing also includes page lookup and softmax.
t is the larger of synchronized host-wall and CUDA-event seconds for the complete call, including dispatch, temporary allocations, writes, and synchronization.

Three-trial median throughputs (total work over total time for decode-step streams) are combined geometrically within each family (decode, spec, long, stream), then families receive equal weight. Preparation, reference checks, and warm-up are excluded.
conditions: All scored and correctness cases must pass.
Preserve BF16 attention, page mapping, shared KV heads, full valid caches, and bottom-right causal masking.
Outputs must satisfy reference tolerances and complete-write checks; preserve inputs and memory boundaries.

sources.paper: Paged-GQA Decode, main.tex:1525–1542; Shared Evaluation Conventions, main.tex:1232–1241

sageattention.label: Dense-equivalent TFLOPS
sageattention.formula:
A = B × L² (noncausal), or B × L(L + 1)/2 (causal)
F = 4 × H_q × d_h × A
q_i = median of 3 trials [F / (10¹² × t)]
S_f = √(GM(recipe) × GM(sweep)) for video, image, llm; S_real = GM of source GMs
score = (S_video × S_image × S_llm × S_real)^(1/4)
details: B is batch size, L sequence length, H_q query-head count, and d_h head width. F is fixed dense-equivalent QK/PV work.

The video, image, llm and real families receive equal geometric weight. In each synthetic family, recipe cases (published default settings) and sweep cases (other supported settings) share it equally; real layers are averaged per source model first.
t is the larger of synchronized host-wall and CUDA-event seconds for smoothing, quantization, attention, dequantization, writes, dispatch, allocation, and synchronization.
Input preparation, compilation/warm-up, and reference checks are excluded.
conditions: All scored, edge, and captured-activation cases must pass.
Global, per-head, and tail errors must meet FP32-reference and calibrated SageAttention limits.
Inputs remain unchanged; evaluation-integrity checks must pass.

sources.paper: SageAttention, main.tex:1544–1564; Shared Evaluation Conventions, main.tex:1232–1241

minference.label: Dense-equivalent TFLOPS
minference.formula:
F(L) = 8192 × L × (L + 1)
q_i = median of 3 prompt trials [F(L_i,j) / (10¹² × t_i,j)]
score = (∏i=1…48 q_i)^(1/48)
details: L is the actual prompt length. The factor 8192 = 2 × 32 query heads × 128 head dimensions counts dense-causal attention work.
The 48 equally weighted cells cover four RULER tasks, three context budgets (32K/64K/128K), and four layers. Each uses median throughput over three prompts.
t is the larger of synchronized host-wall and caller-stream CUDA-event seconds, including pattern estimation, index conversion, attention, repair, output handling, and synchronization.
Model loading, QKV capture, reference checks, and warm-up are excluded.
conditions: All timed and boundary cases must pass.
Against FP32 dense attention, uniform and tail rows require overall NRMSE ≤ 0.25 and worst-head NRMSE ≤ 0.50.
Outputs must be complete and finite; preserve inputs and timing/evaluation integrity.

sources.paper: MInference, main.tex:1566–1583

lmcache.label: KV bandwidth (GB/s)
lmcache.formula:
P_i = Σwaves [(blocks − skip) × kv × NL × BS × NH × W × 2]
b_i = P_i / (10⁹ × median of 3 trial seconds); overlap: b_i × (1 − loss)
G_f = exp(mean over tiers of mean log stratum GM), per family f
G_device = GM(large, small); G_host = GM(large, small, duplex)
score = G_device^0.35 × G_host^0.25 × G_trace^0.10 × G_overlap^0.30
details: P_i is total logical payload. NL = layers, BS = tokens per block, NH = heads, and W = vector width. Split layout uses kv=2 and head width; fused layout uses kv=1 and combined KV width. Elements occupy 2 bytes.
Each transfer counts its payload once; duplex cases count both directions. GB uses decimal 10⁹ bytes.

Trials time the full call sequence using the larger of synchronized host-wall and CUDA-event time. Compilation, preparation, warm-up, and validation are excluded. For overlap cases, loss is the concurrent foreground’s extra time divided by the transfer time, clamped to [0, 0.95].

Cases are averaged geometrically per shape stratum, then per tier (paper, other); tiers count equally in each family. Group weights are 0.35 device (device-large, device-small), 0.25 host (host-large, host-small, host-duplex), 0.10 trace and 0.30 overlap.
conditions: All scored and correctness cases must pass.
Transfers must be bit-exact; preserve sources and untouched destinations across both directions and multi-call traces.
The same-run bandwidth-envelope check must pass.

sources.paper: LMCache KV Block Transfer, main.tex:1585–1604

flash-kmeans.label: Equivalent TFLOP/s
flash-kmeans.formula:
F_assign = 2 × B × N × K × D; F_update = B × N × D
F_full = F_assign + F_update
L = ∏i=1…14 t_i^w_i; C = ∏i=1…14 (F_i / 10¹²)^w_i
native Judge score = L ms (lower is better)
website score = 1000 × C / L ≈ 4694.344299 / L TFLOP/s
details: B = batch size, N = points, K = centroids, D = feature dimension. Assignment and update use their own work counts; combined and deployment cases use F_full. The workload fixes C ≈ 4.694344299 TFLOP.
Group weights are assignment 0.10, update 0.10, full iteration 0.20, fresh-process control 0.10, large-K 0.25, and large-N/high-D 0.25. Divide each group weight equally across its 2/2/4/1/3/2 cases.
t_i is median warmed latency in milliseconds, including dispatch, temporary allocations, GPU work, and synchronization. Preparation, compilation, and reference checks are excluded.
The Judge reports weighted latency L; the paper and website convert it to the weighted geometric mean of effective throughputs.
conditions: All scored and correctness cases must pass.
Preserve nearest-centroid assignment, tie behavior, exact counts, centroid accuracy, and old centroids for empty clusters.
Input integrity, temporary-memory, timing, and fresh-process checks must pass; the full point-by-centroid distance matrix cannot be materialized.

sources.paper: Flash-KMeans, main.tex:1606–1633; equivalent-work conversion checked against website scripts/build_data.py:29–48

mamba2.label: Effective TFLOPS
mamba2.formula:
F = 4 × B × L × H × d_h × d_s
q_i = median of 3 trials [F / (10¹² × t)] (real layers: 1 trial)
G_f = geometric mean of the cases in family f
score = (G_batch × G_serving × G_long × G_real)^(1/4)
details: B is batch size, L sequence length, H heads, d_h channels per head, and d_s state dimension. F counts recurrent state-update and output-projection work.

Four workload families: batch (training-length and padded batches), serving (batch 1 at real request lengths), long (batch 1 from 60K tokens to each model’s context limit) and real (captured layers). Cases have equal weight within a family, and families have equal weight.
t is the larger of synchronized host-wall and CUDA-event seconds for the complete forward call. Three trials are timed after warm-up, each on fresh inputs; a captured real layer is timed once.
conditions: All scored and boundary cases must pass.
Outputs must satisfy FP32-reference elementwise tolerances and relative L2 ≤ 0.006 (captured real layers: relative L2 ≤ 0.013 alone), with complete finite writes and unchanged inputs.
Preserve the recurrence, use TileLang for all computation, and meet warm-up and temporary-memory limits.

sources.paper: Mamba-2 SSD Forward, main.tex:1635–1651; Shared Evaluation Conventions, main.tex:1232–1241

kvpress.label: Output-distribution fidelity
kvpress.formula:
KL(p ∥ q) = Σ_v p(v) ln[p(v) / q(v)]
f(i, ρ) = exp[−Σ_t KL(p_full(i,t) ∥ p_compressed(i,t,ρ)) / n_i]
F(g, ρ) = Σ_{i in family g} f(i, ρ) / |I_g|
score = (100 / 3) × Σ_{ρ in {0.5, 0.75, 0.875}} [Π_{g=1…4} F(g, ρ)]^(1/4)
details: ρ is the eviction fraction: 50%, 75%, or 87.5%. Both distributions use the same full-cache reference continuation of n_i tokens.
Average token KL before exponentiating, then average item fidelities within retrieval, aggregation, QA, and generation families.
Take the equally weighted geometric mean across families, then the arithmetic mean across eviction settings.
The score is 0–100 fidelity points; 100 means identical distributions.
conditions: Selections must satisfy index/cache budgets and preserve inputs; reference continuations contain at least 16 tokens and fidelity is finite.
Selection time is capped at 30% of total prefill and 60% per item/setting; policy memory is capped at 8 GiB.
Inputs and the CPU and CUDA RNG state must be left unchanged.

sources.paper: kvpress KV Eviction — main.tex lines 1656–1682

kvzip.label: Answer-quality retention
kvzip.formula:
a(d, κ) = mean_context_rows(mean_questions(native answer score))
r(d, κ) = a(d, κ) / a(d, 1)
score = (100 / 9) × Σ_{κ in {0.1, 0.2, 0.3}} Σ_{g in G} [Σ_{d in D_g} r(d, κ) / |D_g|]
details: κ is the keep fraction: 10%, 20%, or 30%. a(d, 1) is dataset d’s positive full-cache reference.
Average native answer scores across questions within each context, then across contexts within each dataset. Graders cover answer matching, numerical answers, code retrieval, and summarization.
G contains retrieval, contextual QA, and redundancy. Datasets are equally weighted within groups; groups and keep fractions are equally weighted.
100 denotes full-cache quality on average; scores can exceed 100.
conditions: Scores must be finite FP32 values of the required shape, deterministic, query-agnostic, and preserve inputs.
Scoring time is capped at 25% of total prefill; the per-row cap is max(50% of row prefill, 10 × shortest suite prefill). Memory is capped at 8 GiB.
Each dataset must have a positive full-cache reference.

sources.paper: KVzip KV Scoring — main.tex lines 1684–1701

qvg.label: Quality-weighted KV codec score
qvg.formula:
R_m = total BF16 KV bytes / total stored payload bytes
q_m = (f_m + v_m) / 2
score = √[R_LongCat × (1 + q_LongCat) × R_HY × (1 + q_HY)]
details: Each model pools bytes across all compression calls and cases.
Stored bytes include complete tensor storage and reconstruction metadata; aliased storage counts once within each payload.
Only codec inputs enter the ratio. HY’s newest BF16 chunk and text KV are excluded; LongCat’s condition-frame KV is included.
Frame fidelity f averages normalized PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS improvements over the human codec, each capped at 1 toward the targets 40 dB, 1, and 0.
Video quality v is the minimum normalized VBench margin across four dimensions, minus the human codec's corresponding minimum margin.
Both video models have equal geometric weight. The human codec has q = 0 and a task score of 6.82.
Scores were recomputed after the original runs. Agents optimized the original compression-only metric.
conditions: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and VBench must pass model-average and individual-case quality gates against BF16 references.
Every case must satisfy runtime, compression coverage, correctness, and device-memory limits.
Byte counts must match actual payload storage and BF16 inputs, remain positive, and not exceed original size.

sources.paper: Current author-supplied main.tex: eq:qvg_task_score and app:qvg_quality_score; quality-weighted submission values and source hash in data/qvg_scores.json

eagle3.label: Generated-token throughput
eagle3.formula:
u_c = Σ_{i in calls(c)} emitted_tokens_i / Σ_{i in calls(c)} wall_seconds_i
score = (Π_{c=1…6} u_c)^(1/6)  tokens/s
details: Count newly emitted tokens, including final EOS. Batched calls sum tokens across requests and count wall time once.
Time covers prefill, drafting, verification, acceptance, cache updates, synchronization, and return. Construction, preparation, warm-up, and reference checks are excluded.
Pool tokens and seconds within each of six cells: chat_bs1, math_bs1, code_bs1, longctx_bs1, think_bs1, and mixed_bs8. Combine cell throughputs with equal geometric weight.
conditions: A fresh target checks calibrated greedy consistency; preserve prompts and stopping rules.
Determinism, request isolation, source/model integrity, completion, time, memory, and verified throughput checks must pass.

sources.paper: EAGLE-3 Speculative Decoding — main.tex lines 1725–1741

llada.label: Useful-token throughput
llada.formula:
u_c = Σ_{i in requests(c)} useful_tokens_i / Σ_{i in requests(c)} completion_seconds_i
score = (Π_{c=1…12} u_c)^(1/12)  tokens/s
details: GSM8K, MATH, and MBPP count retokenized completion text after EOS/stop truncation and special-token removal. HumanEval counts non-EOS slots across the generated buffer.
Time covers the complete request: model evaluations, token selection, allocation, cache handling, synchronization, and return. Loading, tokenization, warm-up, text decoding, and grading are excluded.
Each row fixes dataset, few-shot setting, and output length. Pool useful tokens and seconds within each row, then give all twelve rows equal geometric weight.
conditions: Reference-relative correctness, parseability, and token-retention checks apply per row, benchmark, and suite; retention is at least 90% overall and 75% per benchmark.
Useful-token retention above 150% of the reference makes the run invalid; frozen quality thresholds must pass.
Determinism, cache isolation, source/model integrity, complete outputs, timing, memory, and reference qualification must pass.

sources.paper: LLaDA Decoding — main.tex lines 1743–1760

sdv2.label: Latency-weighted FPS
sdv2.formula:
v_i = frames_i(chunks 12…last) / [emit_i(last) − push_i(12)]
ℓ_i = p99{emit_i(k) − push_i(k) : k = 12…last}
s_i = v_i × (ℓ_seed,i / ℓ_i)^(1/4)
score = (Π_{i=1…12} s_i)^(1/12)  FPS
details: Steady-state FPS counts frames in chunks 12 through the end, timed from the push of chunk 12 until the final output is ready on the GPU.
ℓ_i is p99 push-to-emit latency over those chunks. ℓ_seed,i is measured from the unmodified seed in the same evaluation on the same GPUs.
The latency ratio has exponent 1/4. All twelve streams have equal geometric weight, and the score retains FPS units.
conditions: Every latent and frame must match the seed bit for bit, with complete, ordered, causal outputs and correct cleanup.
First-frame latency is capped at max(2.5 × seed, seed + 4 s), p99 at 3 × seed, and construction at max(2 × seed, seed + 60 s).
Memory/runtime checks must pass; each GPU’s peak memory is capped at the larger seed GPU peak + 8 GiB.

serving.label: Valid tool steps / min
serving.formula:
V = Σ_{192 workflows} count(tool.returncode exists and T_start ≤ tool_end ≤ T_start + 1800 s)
score = 60 × V / 1800 = V / 30  steps/min
details: Count tool return records whose completion timestamps fall within the scored window, including its boundaries. Zero and nonzero return codes both count.
The 1,800-second window follows a 300-second warm-up. Steps started during warm-up count if completed inside the window.
Sum steps across 192 concurrent workflows, each capped at 100 valid steps.
conditions: Preserve requests, responses, and streaming behavior with one-to-one backend forwarding.
Protocol identity, request success, valid-step proportion, gateway waiting, backend work per step, and throughput accounting must pass.
